label: Pointer
description: A variable that stores the memory address of another variable.

label: Struct
description: A user-defined composite data type that groups variables under one name.

label: Union
description: A data type where all members share the same memory location.

label: Enum
description: A set of named integer constants used to improve code readability.

label: Lifetime
description: The duration for which a variable exists in memory (automatic, static, dynamic).

label: Thread
description: A unit of execution within a process, enabling concurrent operations.

label: Event
description: An occurrence or signal that triggers specific code execution, often via callbacks.

label: Mutex
description: A synchronization primitive that prevents multiple threads from accessing shared data simultaneously.

label: Semaphore
description: A signaling mechanism used to control access to shared resources.

label: Callback
description: A function passed as an argument to another function, invoked at a later time.

label: Heap
description: Memory region used for dynamic allocation via malloc, calloc, realloc.

label: Stack
description: Memory region used for automatic variables and function call management.

label: Buffer
description: A temporary memory area used to store data during input/output operations.

label: Signal
description: An asynchronous notification sent to a process to trigger a handler.

label: Interrupt
description: A hardware or software mechanism that temporarily halts execution to handle events.

label: Compiler
description: A program that translates C source code into machine code.

label: Linker
description: A tool that combines object files and libraries into an executable.

label: Library
description: A collection of precompiled routines, either static (.a) or dynamic (.so).

label: Header file
description: A file containing declarations and macros, typically with a .h extension.

label: State machine
description: A programming model where behavior is defined by states and transitions.
